question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund is a close-ended Category III AIF (NOT an LVF) with investable funds of INR 600 crore. What is the maximum concentration limit in a single investee company?

answer.text: INR 30 crore (5% of investable funds — open-ended Cat III cap only)
INR 120 crore (20% of investable funds — LVF cap)
INR 150 crore (25% of investable funds — Cat I/II close-ended cap)
INR 60 crore (10% — same for open-ended and close-ended Cat III)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, Category III AIFs — whether open-ended or close-ended — are capped at 10% of investable funds in a single investee company. Thus 10% x INR 600 cr = INR 60 crore. The 20% concession applies ONLY to LVFs of Cat III; Cat I/II close-ended have 25%. The Trap: Option A invents a 5% open-ended-only cap that does not exist in the Regulations. Option B is the LVF-only carve-out. Option C is the Cat I/II close-ended figure. Only option D states the unified 10% Cat III rule that applies to the stated facts. Note: The original item had two options stating "INR 60 crore (10%)" with different rationales, producing answer ambiguity. Option A has been rewritten to a clearly wrong open-ended-only 5% statement so the keyed answer D is now uniquely correct. Source: FINAL_Series-XIX-E_Category III AIF Managers.pdf, p. 404.
